name: Raz–Stamm estriol
question: Does intravaginal estriol cream reduce recurrent urinary tract infection compared with placebo in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Postmenopausal women referred to a single infectious disease clinic after at least three culture-confirmed symptomatic urinary tract infections in the preceding year.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Patient Population and Recruitment; Results, Comparison of the Study Groups

verdictNote: The annualized infection rate was lower with estriol; follow-up lasted eight months.
takeaway: In postmenopausal women with recurrent symptomatic urinary tract infections, intravaginal estriol cream reduced the annualized median incidence of bacteriuria episodes (symptomatic and asymptomatic) versus placebo cream: 0.5 versus 5.9 episodes per patient-year during eight months of follow-up.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Raz R, Stamm WE. "A Controlled Trial of Intravaginal Estriol in Postmenopausal Women with Recurrent Urinary Tract Infections." *N Engl J Med.* 1993;329(11):753-756. doi:10.1056/NEJM199309093291102
